importPdfs.title: Import PDFs
importPdfs.formatHint: Format: Date, Description, Expense, Income, Balance. Only Expenses feed the charts. Duplicates are skipped automatically.
importPdfs.formatHintExtra: Tested with Revolut statements. Numeric dates (dd.mm.yyyy, common at European banks like BIL Luxembourg) are also recognized — if your statement doesn't import correctly, see how to report it in Settings → Data or edit manually in the table.
importPdfs.dragAnywhereHint: You can also drag PDFs anywhere on the dashboard page.

budget.hint: Set a spending target per category — enables "Budget" mode in the dashboard comparison and feeds the cash flow Forecast tab.
budget.footerHint: Categories without a target use the average of recent months in the Forecast — no need to fill in everything.

openingBalance.title: Opening balance
openingBalance.statusNone: No opening balance set — Cumulative cash flow starts from zero.
openingBalance.explanation: If the statement starts partway through (e.g. January/2026) and is missing an entry before it (e.g. December's salary that paid for the start of January), enter here the balance you had one day before the first imported statement. This value feeds both the Current balance (top of the dashboard) and the start of the Cumulative cash flow chart. Alternative: instead of filling this in, log a manual Income transaction in December with the total you had — same result, but don't use both at once or it'll double-count.
